newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares tumble, further losses seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares tumble, further losses seen.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI index lost three percent on Tuesday and traders said another 10 percent of losses could be expected before prices turned the corner.
The 11-share index ended 40.85 points down at 1,288.3.

"It's now clear that no custodian accounts have been opened yet. The market's tired of waiting and the falling trend could gather momentum in the next days," said Goran Spasenic, a trader at brokerage BPH.

The central bank blocked foreign buying last month when it ruled international investors had to open special accounts if they wanted to trade securities. Banks have delayed making the accounts available, blaming lengthy operational procedures.
Market participants agreed the absence of foreign buying was bearish in the short term but some held out the hope that bottom-fishing would bring about an early revivial.
"I believe this is a good time to buy Slovenian shares because the offer is very small and prices will not stay this low forever," one trader said.
An analyst forecast prices would rebound as soon as international investors were able to reenter the market.
"Judging from the phone calls of international investment funds the interest in Slovenian shares is very big," he said.
Bank SKB had the highest turnover on Tuesday. Its shares tumbled 8.15 percent to 47,530 tolars on volume of 731 shares.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, down 8.97 percent to 15,020 on volume of 20 shares.
Preferred shares of trader Kovinotehna were the top gainer, up 9.09 percent to 480 tolars on volume of two shares.
